newsitem.title: ISRAEL: McDonnell Douglas in Israel solar deal.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas in Israel solar deal.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas, Israel's Ormat Industries, Rotem Industries and the Weizmann Institute of Science have been awarded $5.3 million for a solar power plant project, the Weizmann Institute said on Monday.

The U.S.-Israel Science and Technology Commission (USISTC) awarded the funds for the group to demonstrate jointly the commercial feasibility of an advanced solar power plant based on breakthrough U.S.-Israeli technology, it said.
A collaboration agreement between the parties was sealed at the U.S. Space and Rocket Center in Huntsville, Alabama.
"Recent market assessments indicate that this new technology has the potential of wide international applications," Weizmann Institute said in a statement.

The system, capable of generating from hundreds of kilowatts to tens of megawatts of power, uses special optics and an innovative air receiver to reflect, concentrate and convert sunlight to power gas and steam turbines, it said.
In less than three years, the group is to develop an operational 200-300 kilowatt system to be located at Weizmann's solar research facility in Rehovot, near Tel Aviv.

The system will be unique in that production facilities will be on the ground rather than at the top of a tower, concentrators will be able to heat air sufficiently to power advanced gas turbines, and the solar receiver contains hundreds of ceramic pins.
"The collaboration's ultimate goal is to develop an industrial product...that will produce electricity at competitive prices compared with those of existing power stations," it said.
McDonnell Douglas, among its responsibilities, will lead the team.

Ormat specialises in the design, manufacture and worldwide installation of innovative power systems and plants. Rotem has many years of experience in optical design, high temperature materials and engineering.
